I live on a tropical island. Dogs are not really "owned" so much as maintained. There are clubs that feed and provide medical care for adopted dogs. This adoption is shown by a collar. The vast majority of dogs are collared. Dogs come and go in libraries and stores, etc. They do what they want. There's a downside: some dogs get hurt, or get ill. They die somewhat unmourned. I'm not saying it's good or bad.

So, I have a little friend who met me for breakfast every day. She walked with a limp because of a tumor on her foot, but she was adopted. Her collar told me she was "Lolly", and she knew her name. (Most do not know their names.) About three weeks ago, Lolly disappeared. Temperatures into the 40s suggested that she was hiding in someone's air conditioning. After a week, I thought maybe new dogs had run her off. (That's happened before.) I was prepared for the worst. Today, she turned up at breakfast! Yay! She had foot surgery and was more mobile!

I just thought I'd tell people who might appreciate it.
